title: I recreated Tekken 3 in Godot: all fighters, all modes, and the original UI
author: nomadic_ua

comments.author: JJBareaIsLeFather
comments.body: Awesome. I'm working on a similar project for ps1 wrestling games, though not a literal port. Emulation will soon be pointless!

replies.author: nomadic_ua
replies.body:
I don't like emulators - glitchy graphics, awkward controls, and all that - but here, everything is done exactly the way I like it.

I don't intend to distribute the game itself; at most, the source code.

comments.author: sumane12
comments.body: Awesome, but public service announcement, if anyone wants to recreate a game, please improve somethong on it, even if its just thr graphics. Emulators exist.

replies.author: nomadic_ua
replies.body: The graphics have been improved - I tried to get the most out of the original models and textures.

replies.author: sumane12
replies.body:
Yeah the resolution looks much better, and if this is what you wanted, cool.

Theres just no reason to go for this over the original with an emulator. Id have been really excited to see new models and redone environments. But youve always got the option to do that now.

replies.author: nomadic_ua
replies.body:
In addition to higher resolution, there are modern techniques for anti-aliasing, filtering, and lighting, as well as soft, realistic shadows, and so on.

For now, the authenticity of the original game matters more to me than modding.

replies.author: sumane12
replies.body: Fair, if thats what you wanted, well done.

comments.author: sunnystormy64
comments.body: The issue is that you're taking privately-owned IP and doing whatever you want with it. People on this sub (including myself) are going to take issue with this because what you've done will be used as evidence by "flat-earther" politicians to keep AI out of the hands of us plebians. If you're going to use AI for something, please make whatever it is original.

replies.author: cxfoulke
replies.body:
It's also just a scary thing like before decompiling games was enough effort and the skills limited to a small enough subset that it was basically a form of copyright protection. 

Now like basically anyone could yoink your game and publish it... Any unique feature can be ripped and produced for less effort. It's a little sad. 

People used to avoid godot itself just because its easier to decompile and "steal" games. Now it's any game. We're gonna have to shift to always online for everything and start doing very aggressive methods. Or live in a weird world of the only way to protect your stuff is expensive lawyers.
